1935-06-14.text: Tacoma, Wash.—A principle of old English law—that a wife is the mere chattel of her husband—was cited by Tacoma attorneys today as likely to save Mrs. Harmon M. Waley from a life sentence for kidnapping George Weyerhaeuser. While the 19-year-old Mrs. Waley and her ex-convict husband remained incommunicado in the county jail at Olympia, federal agents followed up fresh clues in their intensive search for William Mahan, the third suspect in the $200,000 kidnapping. Near Butte, Mont., they searched a mountain cabin, from which a mysterious occupant was believed to have fled when the owner approached it yesterday. Fingerprints were taken of articles in the cabin to determine if the recent resident might have been the scar-faced Mahan. As Tacomans speculated about the outcome of the federal kidnap trial, attorneys cited a bit of jurisprudence from the middle ages which is an important part of

London, June 14—High British sources today confirmed the fact of an agreement between Great Britain and Germany on the terms of a bilateral treaty restricting the German navy to 35 per cent of the under-age British naval strength. Reichsfuehrer Hitler's assent to the terms was formally communicated this morning to Sir Samuel Hoare, British foreign secretary, at a conference with Joachim Von Ribbentrop, Hitler's armaments expert. Some naval authorities asserted that under these terms the German navy would be actually only 17 percent the size of the British navy at present in view of the great proportion of the British fleet composed of over-age vessels. It was understood, however, that the treaty contemplates the replacement of Great Britain’s over-age vessels within the limits prescribed by the Washington and London naval treaties.

London —(— An authoritative source stated Thursday that Great Britain and France are consulting with Italy in an attempt to draw up a formula for the protection of Italy's “special economic interests” in Ethiopia. It was understood that Italy would like to obtain a protectorate over Ethiopia but that Great Britain seeks to find some other solution to the problem. It was said that neither this matter nor the question of frontier changes is being discussed with Ethiopia. It was pointed out that the recent Geneva agreement prohibits the Italo-Ethiopian conciliation negotiations, which shortly are to be resumed at The Hague, from touching on other subjects until the responsibility for the frontier incidents has been settled. British official quarters emphatically denied that Great Britain's interests at Lake Tsana, one of the sources of the water supply of Egypt and the Sudan, were connected

Shanghai, June 14.—(/)—China was reported planning today to send a special emissary to the United States and England on “a difficult and delicate mission.” Closer contact with those countries on matters in the Far East was described as an object of the visit. The reports also circulated in Nanking, seat of the Nationalist government. Increased tension was reported from Peiping, where Chinese officials said the country faced “the gravest crisis since the Shanghai War of 1932.” Families of many officials crowded railway trains as they began an exodus to the south.

Beckenham, Eng., June 14.— Helen Wills Moody suffered the first defeat of her comeback campaign today when she bowed to Kay Stammers, 6-0, 6-4, in a semi-final match of the Kent tennis championship. Miss Stammers, attractive, hard-hitting and probably one of the ten best women tennis players in the world, entered the semi-final round when she defeated Mrs. Hilsen Bennett Whittingstall, 7-5, 6-4 in the quarter-final bracket.

SANDRINGHAM, England, June 18. —()—King George was reported today to be recovering satisfactorily from an attack of bronchial catarrh. The monarch arose at 7:30 a. m., his usual hour. He planned to spend another restful day at the Sandringham estate.

REGINA, Sask., June 14—(UP)—The vanguard of thousands of relief strikers from British Columbia arrived today in Regina, where the Royal Canadian Mounted Police were under orders to disband the Ottawa-bound marchers. There was no disorder but tension was apparent. Leaders of the marchers said they would not be stopped at Ottawa. Approximately 2,000 marchers were in the group arriving here. Thousands of others were en route from Moose Jaw, the last previous stop. The marchers were directed to the stadium at the exhibition grounds for breakfast.

A dispatch from Omaha says: John J. Wilters, of Omaha, and Charles Wilters, of Milwaukee, 85 year old twins who think they may be “about the oldest twins in America,” held their annual reunion here Wednesday. They were born in Germany and both left home at the age of 14, later serving in the British merchant marine. Charles came to the United States first, with John following several months later. Charles settled in Milwaukee in 1872 and was a city fireman for 37 years before pensioned. John, before coming to Omaha to live with a married daughter, farmed near Le Mars.

1935-05-30.text: LONDON, May 30. (?)—Germany today submitted the draft of a plan for a Western European air pact, and it was authoritatively stated the Reich's suggestion would be answered by the demand that Germany simultaneously join a general armaments and security agreement and return to the League of Nations. Germany's air pact draft was submitted simultaneously to the governments of Britain, France, Italy and Belgium.

London, May 29,—(/P)—An exchange telegraph dispatch said tonight the east side of the island of Formosa, shaken by a disastrous earthquake in April, was slightly damaged early Thursday by another quake, but no casualties were reported. The dispatch, from Taihoku, capital of the Japanese-owned island, reported the shock was centered in the city of Taichu. The island of Formosa was shaken by a heavy earthquake on April 21, when more than 3,000 persons were killed and 10,000 injured.

London, May 29.—Exchange telegraph dispatches tonight said an earthquake similar in intensity to the one in April which killed more than 3,000 had struck the Japanese-owned island of Formosa but that heavy casualties were not expected. The reports said inhabitants who had been engaged in reconstruction were panic-stricken by the new shock and were evacuating. Seismologists were quoted as expressing belief the quake was a sequel to April's, now that the ground has settled.

PARIS, (UP)-- The chamber of deputies finance committee today refused to approve the drastic powers asked by Premier Pierre Flandin to avert a political crisis, protect the franc and balance the budget. - The vote was 25 to 15. A political crisis of the gravest nature threatened. The fall of the government appeared almost certain in the midst of its campaign to save the franc from devaluation, halt the flight of gold from France and restore economic stability. Despite persistent rumors on the bourse that Flandin would resign, the premier’s office tonight insisted that he intends to appear in the chamber tomorrow regardless of the vote. The chamber will debate the proposed powers on which he eventually intends to seek a vote of confidence. The left wing groups in the chamber arranged a meeting for tomorrow morning to decide how they will vote at the afternoon session, but observers doubte

and alleged violations of treaties, i have been delivered to the Chinese national government, it was officially admitted today. The official version of the demands was not available and the details were kept secret here, but it was admitted that Col. Takahashi Sakai, chief of the Japanese garrison at Tientsin, issued the warning. The alleged treaty violations included mention of the Tangku truce and the Boxer protocol of 1901. There were strong indications that the Japanese war lords again would act as they did in September, 1931, when the conquest of Manchuria began and control of the entire policy toward China was taken from civilian hands.

TOKYO, May 30. (UP)—Forty coal miners in the Fukushima prefecture were entombed today by an explosion in the Iriyama mine and their condition was regarded as hopeless. Fifty men were below ground when the explosion occurred at 3:30 p.m. Rapid rescue work succeeded in getting ten of them to the surface unharmed. The situation of the remaining forty was reported as probably beyond help.

| PARIS, 4P—Finance Minister Louis Germain-Martin resigned Thursday night shortly after Premier Pierre-Etienne Flandin, weak and haggard as a result of injuries he suffered recently in an automobile accident, went before the chamber of deputies to lead his government's fight for sweeping powers to defend the franc. Deputies hostile to the government's demand for dictatorial financial powers had concentrated their fire upon Germain-Martin, who has stoutly opposed devaluation of the currency, and his resignation, regarded as an effort to save the Flandin cabinet, was immediately accepted. Resting his fractured left arm on the cushioned support prepared in advance, Flandin lashed out at speculators against the franc and denounced the campaign for devaluation headed by Raymond Patenotre, publisher of the newspaper Le Petit Journal. Flandin announced his finance minister's resignation from th

RIS, May 30—(UP)—Americans and Europeans gathered at the graves of America's war dead today to pay homage to their memory, in France, where some 30,000 soldiers and sailors are buried, French officials and army men joined American veterans and American residents in simple rites. Graves were decorated with American and French flags and brightened with poppies. Flags that had stood at half mast were hoisted to full mast at noon. Impressive services were held in the American Cathedral church here, Dean Frederick W. Beekman repeated the service held on Memorial Day, 1918 when the German armies threatened Paris. Catholic services were held at St. Joseph's church. Later those who attended both services marched to the Arc de Triomphe and placed a wreath on the tomb of the unknown soldier in the name of America. American Speaker Ambassador Jesse I. Straus spoke at the ceremony at Huresnes cemete

1935-05-12.text: London —(P)— More than 500 persons were injured Saturday night as King George and Queen Mary made the last of their nightly jubilee appearances on a floodlit balcony of Buckingham Palace before a surging mob of a quarter of a million persons. Scores of persons were knocked down and many others fainted as the throng pressed against the palace gates. Ambulance men raced from the steps of Victoria Memorial, picking up fallen men, women and children. Twelve persons were removed to hospitals while more than 500 were treated at the field ambulance station. The smiling monarchs remained in view for seven minutes, waving to the cheering crowd, while the crush grew worse every moment and the casualties grew more numerous. Half an hour later, the king and queen appeared again for three minutes in response to the persistent demands of the populace. The king in evening dress, wore a black overcoat a

, AWOMGOT, WAY Shem Usa t Jil Wan authoritatively learned today that Great Britain, alarmed by reports from East Africa and Rome in connection with the Italo-Ethiopian dispute, has initiated new efforts to settle the troubles between the two nations. It was learned that the British are cooperating with the French in making new representations to Rome and Addis Ababa in order to end the difficulties amicably. Informed quarters said the relations between the government of Premier Mussolini and that of Emperor Haile Selassie are rapidly becoming more tense and may flame into war momentarily if there is any careless act on either side. With each country accusing the other of provocative moves, Great Britain is worrying about the League of Nations Council’s consideration of Ethiopia’s appeal which will come up May 20. Informed quarters indicated that Italy probably would walk out of the sessi

(Copyright, 1935, by United Press) Weinsberg, Germany, May 11 (UP) — Grover Cleveland Bergdoll, American draft dodger, today offered to surrender to American authorities and stand trial in federal court provided a five-year court-martial sentence against him is annulled. Bergdoll’s offer came when he was commenting on the court refusal of American authorities to grant his young German wife’s plea that for the sake of their four German-born children he be permitted to return to the United States. “I have not the slightest idea whether President Roosevelt will listen to my wife’s appeal,” he said. “I am willing to go over and surrender and be tried in a federal court provided the court-martial proceedings are annulled.” The offer is a renewal of one he made early in the days when, just after the World War, he escaped from federal soldiers taking him to prison and reached refuge in Germany.

ST. JOHN'S, Nfld., May 12. (AP)—Rioting hoodlums, driven to cover by the batons of 200 reserve policemen, today left in their wake two-score broken, looted store fronts and a badly crippled light and power system. It was impossible to estimate immediately the damage wrought by the crowd of more than 900 jobless who scurried through the city’s main thoroughfares last night. Scores were believed injured as police used their batons freely in their battle to clear the streets.

ADDIS ABABA, Ethiopia, (P)— Ethiopia called upon Benito Mussolini Saturday to show his hand in their six-months-old border quarrel. A source close to the government said mobilization of the black warriors of Emperor Haile Selassie, “conquering lion of Judah,” would be ordered if settlement of all differences is not assured at the meeting of the League council May 20 or if additional Italian divisions continue to pour into neighboring territory. The government renewed Saturday its demand that arbiters of disputed questions be named as provided under a treaty between the two countries. London reports that France and Great Britain were pressing Italy to hasten arbitration were favorably received here. Ethiopians scoffed at Italian reports that Emperor Haile Selassie, now on a trip to Harrar, had gone to inspect frontier war preparations. It was officially announced he has gone to take radiu

TOKYO, May 11. (P—w. 56. Gates, retired United States naval lieutenant held in Formosa on charges of violating the maritime law and suspected of espionage, was freed today after paying a $57 fine on a maritime law violation count. Also freed after paying a similar fine was Gates’ companion, Gen Rubin and a Russian. They had been detained when they landed from a German ketch on the North coast of Formosa.

Metz, France, May 11. (?)—French gendarmes with drawn pistols arrested a German Nazi storm trooper tonight and forced the rest of the detachment back across the frontier after the Nazis crossed the border near Freyming to go to a cafe in French territory. The officer in charge of the Nazis, named Haslingen, was arrested, whereupon his companions sought to release him by force. The gendarmes drew their pistols and the troopers quickly retired, leaving the officer in the hands of the French.

GENEVA, May 11.—(UP)—Officials of the League of Nations received alarming reports today about potential war between Italy and Abyssinia. Information reaching the league indicated that hostilities were imminent, and there seemed no sure way of stopping them by international arbitration. Italy's mobilization of more than 1,000,000 men under the colors, and the war-like statements in the inspired Italian press left little doubt here that Premier Benito Mussolini was ready for action. French and British sources displayed increasing uneasiness. The fear was undisguised that if Italy’s armed strength is diverted to Africa, Germany might seize the opportunity to encroach on Austria, jeopardizing the entire delicate balance of present European relations. Increasing friction between Italy and Abyssinia, punctuated by military preparations on both sides, added to the apprehension here. Italy has b

1935-05-14.text: LONDON, May 14.— (AP) —Miss Angela Joyce, the “Miss England” of 1930, today lost her $500,000 breach of promise suit against Lord Revelstoke, wealthy young banker. A jury in the Old Bailey, which included three women, required only half an hour to reach a verdict for the defendant. Costs of the action were assessed against Miss Joyce. The beauty contest winner, who changed her name from Ivy Dawkins when the stage called to her, testified that Revelstoke, known as Rupert Baring before his father's death, proposed to her several times while he was in school at Cambridge. Once he popped the question in her bedroom, she asserted. This Revelstoke flatly denied, telling the court the question of marriage only came up between them when Miss Joyce herself raised it. He told her he was not interested, he testified.

Ethiopian crisis this afternoon, declared this nation “ready for any eventuality.” Great Britain and France, Italy's good friends, need have no fear lest the steady stream of troops pouring into Africa weaken the country, he said, since “with three classes under arms and a fourth in readiness Italy is ready for any eventuality.” Threaten Mobilization ROME, May 14.—(?)—Italy may have 950,000 troops mobilized by Friday, it was indicated today, as her relations with Ethiopia wavered between conciliation and increased belligerency. A government spokesman, announcing that members of the class of 1912 had received mobilization orders, referred to Ethiopia's “evident attitude of hostility.” He added that while Italy is prepared to name conciliators to attempt to promote a peaceful settlement of the East African dispute under the arbitration treaty of 1928, she would not do so until assurance of

WOOL, England, May 14—Col. T. E. Lawrence, the “Lawrence of Arabia” who led the Arab revolt against Turkey in the World War, lay desperately injured in Wool Military Hospital today. He suffered injuries from which his friends feared he could not recover when on his racing motorcycle he crashed into a bicycle ridden by Albert Hargreaves, 15. It was believed that his leg and skull were fractured, and specialists were consulted in an effort to determine his condition.

Wool, Dorsetshire, Eng.—Col. T. E. Shaw, famed as “Lawrence of Arabia,” who was badly injured last night when his motorcycle crashed into another cyclist, was reported still unconscious but “holding his own.” All relatives of the noted leader of the Arab revolt against Turkish rule during the World War were summoned to his bedside at the military hospital where he was brought last night.

PRU, APU SERA AR ly Me RES PERE ee) —Maj. Gen. J. W. West, honorary surgeon to King George, was called into consultation late this afternoon at the bedside of T. E. Shaw, the famed “Lawrence of Arabia,” who was still unconscious as a result of a motorcycle accident last night in which he was seriously injured. Lawrence’s brother, who was abroad, started to fly home as the author-soldier’s condition continued critical. A bulletin issued shortly after noon by the military hospital where he was taken said he was unconscious but “holding his own.” While strict censorship was clamped down since the accident occurred on war office property, it was understood Lawrence was flung 130 feet from his motorcycle by the force of the impact when his machine struck another cyclist. He was found lying with his left shoulder embedded in the ground. All relatives of the noted leader of the Arab revolt agai

WASHINGTON, (?). Representative Blanton, (D., Tex.), thinks Great Britain's balanced budget is an “infamous lie.” “That budget isn't balanced,” he told the House. “Great Britain owes us a debt of several million dollars, and that budget won't be balanced until that debt is paid.”

WOOL DORSETSHIRE, Eng, May 14 (P).—Col. Thomas E. Lawrence, famed leader of the Arab revolt against Turkish rule during the World War, was reported today to have taken a sudden turn for the worse in the military hospital where he was brought last night after being injured in a motorcycle accident. The staff captain at Bovington Camp near the hospital said the picturesque figure of the Arabian campaign was “in a critical condition and suffering from concussion.” He said he may also have suffered a skull fracture. The accident in which the celebrated figure in Arabia's war-time history was injured occurred last night at Cloud's Hill near Lawrence’s lonely cottage at the north end of Moreton. His motorcycle crashed into a bicycle ridden by a boy and both riders were thrown to the ground. “Lawrence of Arabia,” who emerged from the World War as one of its most picturesque figures, found one o

LONDON — A freak experiment to determine whether a movie racetrack scene would have any effect on a horse nearly wrecked a theater Monday. The horse, a hunter mare, was taken to a private showing of the film and watched calmly while earlier parts of the picture were screened. Once the pictured race got under way, however, the mare picked up her ears, whinnied shrilly, and started a wild rampage, dragging her groom, William Rennie, with her. Twenty seats and stalls were smashed before she could be quieted.

1935-05-03.text: London, May 3.—(AP)—An authoritative source revealed today that a draft of a plan for a western European aviation pact has been drawn up and has been taken into consideration in Paris, Rome, and London simultaneously with the receipt of information in high British quarters that Germany has facilities for building 100 airplanes a month as placements. The British air ministry meeting Reichsfuehrer Hitler's challenge in the air undertook a new program for substantial increases in British fighting plane, airdrome, and royal air force personnel. This program will be presented to parliament within two weeks. The air pact as now drafted is said to include an agreement to call a halt in airplane construction. Well-informed sources stated that the draft thus far has not been submitted to Berlin but that Germany's signature as well as Belgium’s is contemplated. In order to fulfill Prime Minister M

Paris, May 3 (UP)—A hint that a world naval conference might be called for October was given today by Minister of Marine Francois Pietri on his return from a visit to Sir Bolton Eyres-Monsell, British first lord of the admiralty. It was indicated the October suggestion had been made by Eyres-Monsell. The suggestion of a conference came when diplomatic circles here were predicting that there was almost no chance of a successful conference whose motive would be continuation in some form of the Washington naval treaty limiting battleship construction and the London treaty covering the construction of auxiliary ships. Pietri told the United Press he talked to Eyres-Monsell about Germany’s submarine program and he said that this problem would be discussed at the October conference. France was not concerned over the submarine idea. She has 80 post-war submarines, compared to Japan's 68, Italy’

'The subject of aerial warfare occupied the nations of Europe today as Great Britain, France and Italy studied a proposed western Europe aviation security pact in hopes that not only Belgium but Germany could be brought into it. British sources were informed that Germany has developed her military aviation program to such a point that she could build 100 airplanes monthly as replacement in addition to the standard airplane output. The British indicated the possibility that the royal air force would be increased by 200 airplanes immediately, saying such an increase was to maintain parity with the Reich. The air pact draft, it was understood, provided for aerial parity among the nations, much after the fashion of naval treaties.

BERLIN—Air Minister Goering says conscription starts Oct. 1, claims Reich air force equal to any. LONDON—British government announces further air expansion, urges arms limitation, PARIS—France and Russia sign mutual assistance pact. ROME—Italy to send three more army divisions to East Africa.

(Copyright 1935 by The Associated Press) Berlin—(P)—The Polish baron, Georg Sosnowski, regarded by secret police as one of the most dangerous spies in Europe, has been given back to Poland, it was learned today, in exchange for three German spies captured by Poland. It was in the tripping up of Sosnowski that Germany discovered two of its noblewomen, Baroness Benita von Falkenhayn and Frau Renate von Natzmer, were serving as spies against their homeland. The two German women were beheaded February 18, but Sosnowski, a foreigner, was spared to be exchanged for three Germans. As in his capture, a woman also played a part in Baron Sosnowski's release, for one of Poland’s prisoners, given up for the star spy’s safety, was a woman, the beautiful Frau Theodora Ogurek Drazga. The exchange was understood to have been made nine days ago, but the affair was so secret that not a hint was given out

ISTANBUL, May 3 (®.—Five new earthquakes today terrorized the inhabitants of the Kars District on the Turco-Russian frontier and the total number of deaths, including yesterday's casualties, reported at 500 with 1200 injured. Today's tremors were of less violent intensity than the first major shock which destroyed more than 1300 homes, mostly in the Digor District on the Armenian border. The nerve-shattered populace, however, fled from dwelling places into the open countryside, as searchers continued the hunt for victims in the wreckage of 15 towns.

PARIS, May 8 (/).—It was authoritatively learned today that the French will assist Soviet Russia in renovating her western frontier railways and strategic road systems as an immediate result of the accord for mutual assistance between the Paris and Moscow governments. The general army staffs of the two nations are to consult in order to determine Russia's ability rapidly to transport troops in case of need. Plans will be drawn to aid Russia through the use of French army engineers and the sale to Russia of French war materials.

Istanbul, Turkey, May 3 (UP)— Continued violent earthquakes terrorized the population of the Kars region today as rescue workers fought under great handicaps to aid the suffering. Two hundred were reported dead and 500 injured. Thousands of persons huddled without food or shelter all over the region in fields broken by great earth fissures, among animals which perished in the first great shocks. Boulders which plunged down mountainsides blocked roads and added to the difficulty of sending aid to the stricken population. Fifteen villages were reported destroyed.

1935-05-15.text: WOOL, England, May 15 (UP).— Col. T. E. Lawrence remained unconscious today at Wool Military hospital, suffering from a fractured skull. Specialists struggled to save the hero of the Arabs’ revolt in the desert which changed the history of the Near East. His super-strong constitution was all that kept him alive. His condition was so serious that an operation was impossible for the time being. Lawrence sacrificed himself to save the life of Albert Hargraves, 15, butcher's delivery boy. On his famous black motorcycle he was racing Monday near his cottage at Moreton when at a turn called Hell Fire Corner he saw Hargraves. Lawrence swerved his machine just in time. The boy, on his bicycle, was grazed and thrown to the road but was uninjured. So fast was Lawrence going, it was learned today, that he was catapulted more than 40 feet through the air, and crashed on the road with such force that

Rome, May 14.—Benito Mussolini, declaring Italy “ready for any eventuality,” today warned other nations to keep hands off the quarrel with Ethiopia. No one except Italy, he said in an impromptu speech to the senate, “can be the judge in this most delicate matter.” Denying Great Britain and France had taken diplomatic action to prevent Italo-Ethiopian conflict, the Fascist chieftain said those nations need not be alarmed lest Italy weaken herself in Europe by sending thousands upon thousands of troops into Africa. “We shall maintain under arms for all the time necessary,” he declared, “the three classes of 1911, 1913 and 1914. Moreover, another class, that of 1912, is in reserve and ready.” Mobilization orders went out to parts of the class of 1912 and army headquarters indicated the nation’s men under arms would be pushed almost to the million mark by the end of the week. “I believe a to

Wool, Dorsetshire, Eng. — (VW) — Col. T. E. Lawrence's condition was reported as extremely critical today at the Camp Bovington military hospital, although his strength was being maintained. The famous figure in Great Britain's military history suffered a fractured skull in a motorcycle accident. Physicians attending the wartime leader of the Arabian desert revolt against the Turks said his condition was still too critical to permit an operation. An honorary surgeon to the king came here from Bournemouth to aid in caring for Lawrence, who was injured when he swerved his motorcycle to avoid colliding with a bicycle ridden by a boy, who also was being treated for concussion and shock.

Wool, Dorsetshire, Eng., May 14 ()—As desperate a fight as ever "Lawrence of Arabia" waged on the desert was fought today by the king’s honorary surgeon to save the life of the famed war-time figure, his skull fractured in a motorcycle accident. The military hospital at Covington camp, where T. E. Shaw, known as Colonel Lawrence, lies unconscious, announced that "it is now ascertained that Shaw has a fractured skull." A hospital attache said his condition is very serious. The authorities maintained a strict silence regarding the details of last night’s accident. It was apparent that Shaw was traveling at a terrific speed when his vehicle shot around "Hellfire corner" at Moreton Heath and collided with a 15-year-old cyclist with such a violent impact that Shaw was catapulted 120 feet. Acquaintances of the mystic figure, the so-called British "Haroun Al Raschid," recalled that he once cras

New York, (P)—Harry Winston, New York diamond merchant, today announced his purchase in London of the Jonkers diamond, the largest uncut diamond in the world, for a sum “in excess of $700,000." The stone weighs 726 carats, and is approximately the size of a hen's egg. It will be brought to America within a month or so and displayed to prospective purchasers... If a buyer cannot be found for it, the diamond will be cut into several smaller stones, according to Winston. The Jonkers was unearthed in the South African field on Jan. 16, 1924 by a Negro digger for Jacobus Jonkers, a 62-year old poverty stricken Boer prospector who had worked the field for 15 years without any appreciable success. Jonkers, according to Winston, sold his discovery to the diamond corporation at a reported price of £75,000. It was taken to London where it was viewed by King George and Queen Mary. A move to buy the

WOOL, Dorsetshire, Eng. May 15. (Wednesday) (?U-The nerves of steel that saw Lawrence of Arabia through revolt in the desert stood by him early today after his physicians announced he had taken a turn for the worse. His condition was called “extremely critical.” A specialist from a London hospital said his condition was too serious to permit an operation, and he was still unconscious—but he was given a chance to live. As desperate a fight as ever Col. Thomas E. Lawrence ever waged on the Arabian desert was fought today by the king’s honorary surgeon to save the life of the famed wartime figure, his skull fractured in a motorcycle accident.

London, May 15.— (#) —Lord Rothmere branding the British government's plan to expand the Royal Air Force by 1,000 planes as 'childish and useless for defense' told the House of Lords today, 'I say with full responsibility that Germany at the present moment has 10,000 bombing planes.' The Reich's bombers, the newspaper publisher said, are 'of long range and high speed capable of carrying a ton of high explosives.' His statement created a sensation in the upper house even though Lord Rothermere's Daily Mail has been pounding away at Britain's lack of air defenses and has claimed repeatedly that Germany has a secret air force running into five figures. Lord Rothermere described Germany as 'a growing military power far superior in strength, far superior for offensive purposes and full of aggression which may take at any time a hostile attitude in regard to this country.'

Premier Benito Mussolini's “hands off" dictum concerning Ethiopia, delivered before the Italian senate yesterday, left Great Britain today still determined to do everything possible to prevent hostilities in East Africa. London: It was understood Sir Eric Drummond, British ambassador to Rome, was seeking further consultation with Italian authorities, although his efforts were temporarily unsuccessful. Addis-Ababa: Ethiopian officials said Il Duce’s fiery speech contained nothing new, being merely an official statement of the policy Italy had followed for some time. Paris: French and English discussions with Italy concerning Ethiopia were “just friendly conversations not constituting diplomatic action,” semi-official French sources said as informed observers expressed the belief Mussolini would carry through his Ethiopian plans. Vienna: Government quarters said they took Mussolini's speec

1935-06-20.text: LONDON--() — British officials, equipped with the bargaining power of the new naval agreement with Germany, prepared today to receive delegations of naval experts from France, Italy and Russia with whom they expect to discuss the terms of a proposed multilateral treaty for naval limitation. Well-informed British quarters stated an invitation for the discussion of such a general pact already has been extended to France and that the details probably will be arranged when Capt. Anthony Eden, minister for League of Nations affairs, confers with Premier Pierre Laval, of France, in Paris, on Friday. Despite the clamor raised in the French press over the Anglo-German agreement, British officials insist the French Government officially has expressed neither approval nor disapproval of the agreement. French fears that Britain's next move will be a bi-lateral air pact with Germany were ridiculed b

London—UP—The United States embassy announced today 11 American debutantes and matrons, including Helen Jacobs, the tennis star, will be presented to King George and Queen Mary June 25 in the season's third royal court. Those to be presented at Buckingham Palace by Mrs. Robert W. Bingham, wife of the United States ambassador, are: Mrs. Henry Bedford, New York; Miss Huldah Warfield Cheek, Nashville, Tenn.; Miss Emlen Knight Davies, Miss Cynthia Davis and Miss Marianna Dunn, Washington; Miss Jacobs, Berkeley, Calif. Miss Frances Lorillard Ronalds, Miss Leta Clews and Miss Jane Watson, New York; Miss Nancy Symington, Baltimore, Md.; Miss Priscilla Taylor, Westchester, Pa.

(Copyright. 1935, by The Associated Press!) Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, June 20—Ethiopia's tribal warriors cast aside their shoes today, ready to “defend the empire to the last man” against an anticipated Italian invasion. European military advisers had tried to introduce the footwear, but the troops reverted to bare feet while plunging with almost fanatical fervor into a new, voluntary military training program. “The shoes have been abandoned because agility and mobility were impaired,” a high official said. “They were also an unnecessary expense. When the time comes, our soldiers will fight with bullets, spears and sabres—not with their feet! What they lack in skill in handling machine guns and other implements of modern warfare, the native warriors make up in the fierceness with which they wield sabres. Some 100,000 of the 800,000 men estimated to be available for the field rely almost ent

Sydney, Australia, June 15—(4:— A hurricane, accompanied by a minor earthquake, killed two persons in New South Wales today. The hurricane swept the New South Wales coast, leaving a trail of devastation and changing the configuration of many beaches.

Rome, June 20 (#) — The foreign office was informed today that an Ethiopian aviator tore an Italian flag from an Italian legation automobile in Addis Ababa Tuesday night and attacked the chauffeur. The automobile was that of G. Mombelli, first secretary of the Italian legation to Ethiopia. The affair was stated to be regarded as a diplomatic incident, resulting in the Italian minister filing a strong note of protest with the Ethiopian government. It was indicated the alleged insult to the Italian flag was regarded gravely and that much would depend on what satisfaction the Ethiopian government gave.

| PARIS, June 20.—The Bank of France today reduced its discount rate from 6 to 5 per cent, reflecting lightening of pressure on the French franc. The bank also reduced its rate on advances on securities loans for thirty days from 6 per cent to 5 per cent. Recently the franc had risen above the gold export point largely because of efforts of the government of Pierre Laval to curtail expenditures and balance the budget.

Rome, June 20. (UP)—The Italian minister at Addis Ababa protested to the Abyssinian government today against an incident in which an Italian diplomat was insulted. The foreign office confirmed reports that Giulio Mombelli, first secretary of the Italian legation, parked his automobile outside a cinema and an Abyssinian aviator tore the Italian tri-color from the machine. The chauffeur and the aviator then had a fist fight. Police arrested the Abyssinian.

PARIS, June 20—(AP)—The Bank of France today started to relieve the tight money market by reducing its discount rate from 6 per cent to 5 per cent. In its fight against speculation, the bank increased its rate three times late in May, keeping the high rate for three weeks during the fall of two cabinets and the raid on reserve gold which saw withdrawals of 1,054,000,000 francs in gold in a week. The rate of loans on securities was also reduced today from 6.5 per cent to 6 per cent. The rate on 30-day loans was reduced from 6 per cent to 5 per cent.

1935-05-16.text: WOOL, Dorsetshire, Eng, May 16.--Col. T. E. Lawrence, the famed Lawrence of Arabia, was gradually growing weaker this evening with slight hope held for his recovery from injuries suffered in an accident Monday. Attaches at the military hospital where he was taken Monday night after his motorcycle collided with another cyclist said the leader of the Arab revolt in the desert was sinking.

LONDON--(P)—Viscount Cecil of Chelwood, attacking Premier Mussolini for his Ethiopian policy, declared Thursday Italy could not fairly criticize German rearmament if she ignored her own League of Nations vows. Lord Cecil delivered his attack soon after the government called home Sir Eric Drummond, the British ambassador to Rome, to report on the outcome of recent Anglo-French overtures for peaceful settlement of the East African dispute. It was indicated that Great Britain is determined to continue her efforts to avert hostilities between Italy and the African kingdom in spite of Il Duce's warning that the other powers must not interfere with his projects in East Africa. The question of whether Great Britain might close the Suez Canal and British ports to Italian warships and transports was receiving increased attention among Liberal and Labor political circles.

LONDON, May 16 (F)—Reports of conflict within the cabinet on Britain's foreign policy today revived prediction that changes in the national government were imminent. Political attacks centered on Sir John Simon, foreign secretary, his opponents citing particularly his alleged pro-German sympathies and indications that he had antagonized Premier Mussolini of Italy, inspiring Il Duce's “hands off” speech concerning Ethiopia this week. On the other hand, Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald's recent display of sternness toward Germany boomed his stock for the foreign office, with Stanley Baldwin, lord president of the council, regarded as MacDonald's likeliest successor. Some political observers said they believed MacDonald's first move, if he became foreign secretary, would be to summon another world economic conference. Secretary Hull's statement yesterday that the United States stands ready t

WOOL, Dorsetshire, England, May 35 (Pi)—In a trance-like state, Col. T. E. Lawrence clung to life today, still unconscious at 10 p. m., 58 hours after his skull was fractured in a cycling accident. A staff of Britain's leading brain specialists, including Major General J. W. West, honorary surgeon to the king, worked over the broken body of "Lawrence of Arabia," at Camp Bovington military hospital. The specialists announced Lawrence’s condition is unchanged but the outlook is a little brighter. They agreed the crisis in the life of the romantic World War figure is to be expected within 24 hours.

Wool, England, May 16.—Col. T. E. Lawrence—Lawrence of Arabia—approached a crisis today and hope for his recovery was remote. He was still unconscious, three days after a motorcycle accident in which he suffered a deadly fractured skull, a lacerated brain, a fractured leg and other injuries. This morning's bulletin said: “Mr. Shaw (the name under which Lawrence served in the Royal Air Force) is still unconscious. He passed a fair night. His condition if anything is a little weaker but he is holding his own well.” Surgeons expected a definite turn. It was impossible to operate, he could not even be fed because of his condition, and the remarkably strong physique for which he is noted alone kept him alive. Lawrence, who led the revolt of the Arabs in the World War and after it, served an enlistment in the Royal Air Force as an air-craftsman, was injured Monday when he was thrown 100 feet f

Wool, Dorsetshire, Eng.--(AP)--Grave anxiety was felt today for Col. T. E. Lawrence as he approached the crisis in the injuries he received in a cycling accident Monday. With Lawrence still unconscious at midafternoon seventy-two hours after the accident, his brother, A. H. Lawrence, hastened to the Boyington camp military hospital and waited just outside the patient's room. “I'm afraid the chances for his recovery are very slender,” his brother said this afternoon.

Southampton, Eng—(P)—A woman passenger aboard the Bremen was robbed of jewelry valued at 6,000 pounds (approximately $29,000) shortly after the ship sailed from New York, Feb. 8, it was revealed Thursday when Southampton police were asked to assist in investigating the robbery.

Seville, Spain, May 16 (UP)—Juan Ignacio Pombo, 21-year-old Spanish aviator, started today on a trans-Atlantic flight—to see his sweetheart in Mexico City. Pombo took off at 5:55 a.m. today for Villa Cisneros, in the Rio De Oro country on the west coast of Africa. Thence he will continue to Dakar to take off for Natal, Brazil, to follow the South and Central American coast northward to Mexico. His flight is the result of a promise to his sweetheart, a 19-year-old girl whose name he has not disclosed. She left Spain several months ago with her parents to reside in Mexico City, and Pombo promised her he would fly across to visit her. He has a monoplane which he originally named Emerald Coast. In planning his flight, he conceived the idea of getting backing, renamed the plane the Santander, and won the enthusiastic support of his hometown people to make his flight one that would not only fu

1935-04-10.text: SOUTHAMPTON, England, April 10 (W.P.J)—The trans-Atlantic liner Aquitania went aground today off Brambles Bank in Southampton water. A 50-mile-an-hour gale was blowing when the veteran liner went aground, en route home from New York. Nine tugs sped to the aid of the big ship and were standing by her.

Sir John Simon's summary of Germany's security demands, given before the British House of Commons yesterday, overshadowed last minute preparations in London, Paris and Rome for the momentous tri-power conference at Stresa, Italy, opening tomorrow. The British Foreign Secretary told the Commons that Adolf Hitler, among other things, wants equality of land and air armaments, a navy of about 400,000 tons, a non-aggression pact, no "eastern Locarno," no mutual assistance pact with Russia, no non-aggression pact including Lithuania until the Memel question is satisfactorily settled. The British and French cabinets completed their Stresa proposals and Premier Mussolini of Italy remained at Rocca Delle Carminade. LONDON, April 10. (U.Ph)—Reports that France and Russia were about to enter a virtual military alliance brought a last minute change in British plans for the Stresa conference, it was understood today. The cabinet held an extraordinary meeting just before the British delegation, headed by Ramsay MacDonald, prime minister, and Sir John Simon, foreign secretary, left for Stresa. It was indicated, as a result of the alliance report, that the British at Stresa would try to switch France toward either: merging its Russian agreement into a broader European security system or surrounding it with other treaties to which Germany could adhere. Such a substitute would be based—as is the reported French-Russian agreement—on the penalty clauses of the League of Nations covenant. Just before the cabinet meeting, Simon, in a long talk with American Ambassador Robert Worth Bingham, outlined the European

LONDON, April 10 (AP).—Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald and Sir John Simon, foreign secretary, left by special airplane today for Paris on their way to Stresa, Italy, and the opening tomorrow of the Tripartite conference on Europe's peace problems. The two British statesmen will spend the remainder of the day in Paris, departing from there for Italy on a night train. With them they carried a plan for an all-inclusive European security system which they will propose to the French delegation and their Italian hosts. Before he entered the plane, Mr. MacDonald said: “We are starting on a mission of international good will and cooperation united with security and peace. I hope with all my heart we will be successful. We shall certainly try to be.” An authoritative source stated the British will inform the French and Italians that they are willing to have Great Britain become an active member o

Twenty-six days after Hitler's denunciation of that treaty, which until now had held the continent together like haywire around a ramshackle automobile, Europe's leaders have just reached the point of their first joint conference to decide what to do. (COPYRIGHT, 1930, BY THE ASSOCIATED PRESS) BERLIN, April 10—The same medieval battle-axe which fell on the necks of two noblewomen spies six weeks ago lopped the heads today from two men accused of a crime committed out of political hatred. Sally Eppstein, a 28-year-old Jew, and Harms Ziegler, a 34-year-old Aryan, went to the execution block in Ploetzensee prison’s gloomy courtyard for the slaying of Horst Wessel, the martyred bard of Nazism. Once more the 67-year-old official executioner donned his top hat, kid gloves and tail-coat to perform his gruesome task. The two prisoners had been informed at 6 p.m. last night to prepare “for your last 12 hours.” At the same time the heavy death-cell doors were opened for the night to enable the wardens, whose duty it is to entertain death candidates during their last moments, to keep the doomed men from falling asleep. BERLIN, April 10.—()—General Hermann Wilhelm Goering, Reichsminister, and Frau Emmy Sonnemann, 38-year-old actress, were married today in a 13-minute ceremony in Berlin's city hall. Reichsfuehrer Hitler, clad in his brown uniform, was one of the two groomsmen. A vast crowd, in City Hall Square standing on rooftops and craning necks from windows, shouted itself hoarse as the bridal couple entered the municipal building. No spectators were admitted to the ceremony, however, except members of the wedding party. The marriage was solemnized by tall Mayor Heinrich Sahm, clad in a somber Prince Albert coat and top hat with the heavy golden chain of his office hung about his shoulders. He was assisted by Julius Lippert, state commissioner for Berlin. An honor company of police bearing rifles presented arms and a police band played as the bridal party emerged from city hall. 1935-01-12.text: TORONTO, Jan. 12—(?)—Lloyds of London, which underwrites everything from ocean liners to weather, has refused to insure the Dionne quintuplets, it was reported here today. The guardians of the famous infants were reported to have approached Lloyds after turning down offers of several Canadian and United States companies to insure them for $1690 each, the limit allowable under the insurance law. Attorney General A. W. Roebuck, however, has expressed himself as opposed to insurance for the children. If they live, Roebuck says, insurance will be of no use to them and if they die it will not be needed.
By United Press LONDON, Jan. 11—Emperor Kang Teh of Manchukuo is gravely ill and a regency council has been appointed to rule for him, an Exchange Telegraph Dispatch from Singapore reported today.

HOLLYWOOD, Jan. 12-1 Mary Pickford, screen star, remained in seclusion to-day as Hollywood sought to link her name romantically with Buddy Rogers, former film star, who is now an orchestra leader in London. Miss Pickford obtained a divorce Thursday from Douglas Fairbanks, the swashbuckling hero of many a celluloid drama. In 1920 she obtained a divorce from Owen Moore, also of the films. Although reports persisted in Hollywood that a romance exists between Miss Pickford and Rogers, the star's personal representative took it upon himself to deny there was anything to the reports. “Miss Pickford and Rogers are just good friends,” the representative said. “She has known Rogers and his family for many years, but there certainly is no possibility of a romance between the two.” Doug Has Nothing To Say Rogers, in London, also denied the Hollywood reports, declaring the reports he would marry Mis

| BOSTON, Jan. 12--(UP)—New England floods claimed six lives and caused damage estimated at thousands of dollars before cessation of steady rains and a drop in temperature definitely ended fear today that the disastrous 1927 flood would be repeated in midwinter, Forecast of clear and colder weather over the weekend brought assurance of safety to harassed residents along the banks of surging rivers. Three of the flood victims perished in Connecticut, two in Rhode Island and one in Vermont.

Leipzig, Germany—(taA)— The possibility was seen Friday, through inquiries here, that Detective Arthur Johnson of New York, is taking to the United States Hanna Fisch, Commissioner Spaude of the Leipzig police force, and a former corporal who trained Bruno Richard Hauptmann in the German army. The American detective and three unidentified companions—reported at that time, however, to be a man and two women—sailed Tuesday from Le Havre aboard the S. S. Ile De France for the United States. Commissioner Spaude was Johnson’s right hand man in the investigations conducted by the American policeman at Leipzig into the past of the man who is on trial in Flemington, N. J. Johnson delved most deeply into the history of Isidor Fisch, the man who Hauptmann claimed gave him the Lind- Whether Isidor’s sister, Hanna, is of the party remains a matter of doubt since the family will admit nothing, but it

PARIS, (AP).—Police clashed today with 1,200 communists, members of a “hunger army” attempting to march on Paris. A wall of mobile guards turned back the attempted invasion just west of the city’s outskirts. The demonstrators engaged in a general scuffle with the gendarmes, but found themselves no match for their opponents. Quickly dispersed, the communists said they would make another attempt to enter the city later today after they had been reinforced by the department of Seine-Et-Oise. The communist party organized the advance on Paris from four sides as a gesture to compel the government to extend the dole to thousands of unemployed who they assert are receiving no aid.

Toronto, Jan. 11. (INS) — The Dionne quintuplets will have a fortune of $100,000 by the time their guardians’ contract expires in 1936, it was estimated by officials here to-day. They said the majority of the money is coming from motion pictures and news syndicates. It was also predicted the quintuplets, who were born in the most humble surroundings, would receive further funds when they became older and strong through public appearances, which are banned for the present, but will probably be permitted later.
Astrakhan, U.S.S.R., Jan. 12.—After being marooned for 10 days on an ice floe in the Caspian Sea, 89 fishermen escaped Friday over an ice bridge pointed out to them by airplanes.

Most of the specialists, it was stated, formerly served in the gun or powder rooms of Italian — the opinion was expressed in informed circles that the navy was preparing for possible "events" in the case the League of Nations decides to impose an oil embargo against Italy. It was expected such action, if taken, would be under the leadership of Anthony Eden, Great Britain’s foreign secretary.

Oklahoma City, Dec. 26—A second oil well near the governor's mansion and Oklahoma's state capitol was drilled in today for an initial test of 250 barrels of oil an hour and an estimated 8 million cubic feet of gas a day. The well is the British American's Mary Green, three blocks north of the mansion. The well was completed at 6,354 feet in the Wilcox sand which was topped at 6,319 feet. Although the Mary Green was the discovery well of the capitol area and averaged 150 barrels of oil an hour when it drilled down to 6,365 feet recently, it was shut down when a swab hung up in the well. It then was plugged back to 6,275 feet and another hole started from that point. Last week the British American’s No. 1 Piersol, a block north of the governor’s mansion, was drilled in for an estimated 550 barrels of oil an hour and 20 million cubic feet of gas daily. - LONDON, Dec. 25,—(P)—Two far-reaching projects for the abolition of “Queen Anne's bounty” and to permit the state purchase of coal mining royalties are hailed triumphantly by socialists as “the forerunner of doom for England’s feudal system.” The two measures are calculated by their proponents to lift the age-old burden of “land tithes” from long-suffering farmers, and to free miners from the yoke of private ownership which has restricted them to an average wage of $11 a week. Sir Thomas Inskip, attorney general, announced the government plan to buy out the owners of mining royalties. Shanghai, China (AP) — The Japanese military declared today that the assassination of Tang Yu-Jen, pro-Japanese vice minister of Chinese railways, "throws a dark shadow over the future of Sino-Japanese relations." Chinese authorities immediately declared martial law throughout Shanghai and Nanking. Severe military restrictions were imposed at Hankow against anti-Japanese demonstrations. Tear Up Railroad The Nanking government ordered a section of its railway line torn up in a drastic measure to check the attempt of Shanghai students, protesting the movement for North China separation, to reach the capital in a stolen train. The students seized a locomotive here when authorities refused to grant them free transportation to Nanking, and reached Changchow about 75 miles short of Nanking. Addis Ababa, Dec. 26—(2/— The Ethiopian government reported today that its soldiers had shot down an Italian airplane at Daggah Bur. The airplane was flying in a reconnoitering expedition in company with another. It was brought to earth, according to the government, at 9 a. m., today. Officials reported from Harar that the pilot—not immediately identified—was beheaded.

PARIS, DEC. 26. (AP) — Premier Pierre Laval told his cabinet today, it was reported in the chamber of deputies lobbies, that France would refrain from making any military or naval move toward Italy unless Italy gave provocation. Details of the Premier's future policy to keep out of war and to settle the Italo-Ethiopian conflict were not yet decided, however, informed sources said after Laval met his ministers to draft his defense for tomorrow's chamber of deputies interpellation on foreign policy. TARA, Ethiopia (UP) — Ethiopian forces shot down an Italian plane at Daggah Bur today. The plane was forced down six miles south of Daggah Bur by rifle fire from Ethiopians hiding in a big pit. Two of the occupants of the plane escaped. A third was captured and was reported to have been decapitated. The plane was one of two which flew over Daggah Bur at 5 a.m. seeking out the Ethiopian positions. Apparently seeing nothing, they flew low and the Ethiopians crept out of the pit and opened fire. At noon two more planes arrived, looking for the men who had crashed.

1935-02-13.text: AUSTIN, June 5.—(#)--The Court of Criminal Appeals today affirmed a 12-year sentence assessed Ruby Britain for the murder of Horace Nichols, Seymour banker, in Baylor County last Aug. 15. Miss Britain, 39, a divorcee, testified she shot Nichols, assistant cashier of the First National Bank of Seymour, on a road when she encountered him with another woman. She pleaded self-defense. She testified Nichols had professed love for her and they had had intimate relations, after which, the court noted, she learned of his clandestine meetings with other girls. Nichols was married. The court, on the state’s motion, reversed its previous opinion and affirmed the conviction of Ikey Weatherred, sentenced in Johnson County to eight years for fatally shooting John Green, Cleburne filling station operator, in an altercation May 16, 1934. WASHINGTON, (UP).—Eight major dirigible disasters since 1921 have taken 267 lives in addition to two lives lost in the Macon disaster. January, 1921— British R-34, moored at Howden, England. Ripped to pieces by gale. No lives lost. August, 1921—ZR-2, built in England for the United States, burst into flames over Hull, England. Forty-four dead. February, 1922—semi-dirigible Roma, purchased from Italy by the United States, burned over Hampton Roads, Va. Thirty-four dead. December, 1923—French D'x.

San Francisco, Feb. 12.—(AP)—The British cruiser Australia will stand by the Seth Parker, disabled in the South Seas, until an American naval tug arrives, Phillips Lord, master of the schooner, messaged today. Lord also quoted Commander McLeod of the Australia as declaring the SOS calls from the schooner were genuine and not a publicity stunt. "I realized what you have been through," Lord quoted Commander McLeod as saying, "and am satisfied there never has been any question of you calling upon me unnecessarily. Goodbye and good luck." The Australia had taken aboard nine members of the distressed vessel's crew, but shortly afterward the captain, instead of steaming away, decided to remain in the vicinity until the U. S. S. Ontario arrived. The Ontario left Pago Pago, American Samoa, Monday, and steaming at 12 knots will require about 72 hours to reach the Seth Parker. The disabled ship wi

LONDON, Feb. 13 — Both Great Britain and France, it was indicated in official circles today, have let King Haile Selassie of Ethiopia know they consider it advisable for his country to meet Italy's demands as quickly as possible. Ethiopia's flat denial of Italian charges as published yesterday is regarded critically by officials here, who believe Ethiopia is making a grave error in adopting these tactics. Great Britain and France have known for a long time of the Italian demands, just made public, and are understood to be satisfied that Premier Mussolini's government has been subjected to extreme provocation.

British and French diplomats worked hand in hand at Rome and Addis Ababa Tuesday to avert war in Africa as Ethiopia's diplomatic representative in Rome said flatly his nation would pay not one cent indemnity for Italians slain along the Italian border. Although official circles in London expressed confidence Benito Mussolini would act with moderation and Italo-Ethiopian peace negotiations went forward at Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian government was reported to have massed 30,000 men along the frontier, while Italy had 250,000 ready for call to the colors. ROME—The Ethiopian charge d'affaires said his nation has 1,000,000 men available to fight Italy, asserting Ethiopia expects no foreign ally and needs none. BERLIN, Feb. 13 (4.--German officials said today that Reichsführer Hitler would ask the allied powers for a plebiscite in Austria to determine whether that nation desires to join Germany as a condition to Germany's agreement to a pact guaranteeing non-intervention in Austria.

KAMENZ, Germany, Feb. 13. UP —The aged mother of Bruno Richard Hauptmann, convinced her son would be acquitted of the charge of murdering the Lindbergh baby, eagerly awaited the jury's verdict. She said, “They simply cannot condemn a man without the slightest bit of positive evidence. I’m sure justice will win because everything is on his side.

In the face of the assertion of the Ethiopian charge d'affaires, Negradas Yesus, that 1,000,000 Ethiopians will resist any Italian invasion, informed quarters said Italy is thoroughly determined to settle her score with the African empire unless Addis Ababa furnishes abject satisfaction. Labatt, wealthy London brewer, | If convicted the Cincinnati bookmaker, arrested by United States authorities last September, would be liable to a maximum prison term of 25 years, In sending the jury to hear the prosecution testimony, Justice G. F. McFarlane said the charge it was to consider was a “serious crime, but happily not prevalent in Canada.” Meisner will appear for trial tomorrow morning. Two of the charges relate to the kidnapping and holding of Labatt, and the third accuses him of robbery under arms. Conviction under the latter charge could carry a flogging in addition to the sentence,

BERLIN, Jan. 29 (AP)-- Richard Roiderer, naturalized American citizen whose home is in Chicago, will be indicted tomorrow or Thursday on a charge of treason, it was announced today. Roiderer, it was said, will be brought before the Volksgericht (the people's court) as the first American to be tried by that star chamber court. At the special request of the American embassy, one consular representative will be permitted to attend, but the embassy will not have an opportunity to examine the indictment before trial. Roiderer was brought to Moabit prison in Berlin several days ago after being held under arrest in Munich since June 22, 192.

- BERLIN, Jan. 30—(AP)— Reichsführer Adolf Hitler, commemorating proclaimed: "In the first half of the four year period which I asked the nation to give me to develop my working plan, more than two-thirds of what I has been carried out." "No democratic government in the world can submit itself with greater confidence and hope to a national vote than can the national assumption of power was no less a turning point in history than the socialist government of Germany." Hitler declared that the Nazis’ assumption of power was no less a turning point in history than the World War and that multitudes had the desire to work for peace with honor.

A Baby Grows Up Senate’s Good News Five Little Girls $4,880,000,000 Fifty-three years ago a good American mother, weak but happy, received in her arms a small baby, with pink face and little hair. That baby now lives in the White House, face bronzed by ocean air, hair thick at fifty-three years of age. The baby has grown to be Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States. One hundred and twenty-five million Americans are grateful to his mother, who, happily, has lived to see her son move up, from the cradle in which she first placed him, to the earth’s most important place among men. Congratulations and thanks, first of all, to President Roosevelt’s mother, good wishes, congratulations, and a long life to President Roosevelt. TOKYO, Jan. 30.—A rising tide of military expenditures may face the Japanese people for many years to come, the war lords told the house of representatives today. Replying to a question of when the nation might expect a reduction in the burden of its military preparations, Mineo Osumi, minister of navy, and General Senyuro Hayashi, minister of war, indicated the 1935-36 army and navy budgets must be increased. Hayashi, citing the menace of Soviet activities near Manchoukuo’s frontiers, intimated that Japanese forces in Manchoukuo would be increased. Osumi asserted the navy must construct 50,000 tons of new warships annually from the fiscal Year 1936-37 onward.

BERLIN, Jan. 30—(UP)—Adolf Hitler, in a proclamation marking the second anniversary of his accession to power, today challenged democratic governments to match his accomplishments. “On Jan. 30, 1938, I asked the German people for four years in which to accomplish our first work program,” Hitler said, “in the first half of this term, two thirds of all that I then promised has been accomplished. “No democratic government in the world, therefore, can go to its voters with greater trust and confidence than Germany's national socialist government.” Kurt Schmitt resigned formally today as minister of economics. The proclamation explained there were no celebrations today because of the death of President Paul Von Hindenburg, but that huge nationwide celebration would be held on March 1, marking the return of the Saar to Germany. GAPS AARP AGAMA AV TOKYO, (Thursday) Jan 5, 1981. (AP) — Rengo Prep news agency reported early today in a dispatch from Welsking, Manchukuo, that a Japanese-Manchukuoan force last night captured Kalkha Miao along the Manchu-Mongol border and that the Mongols were retreating to the southward.

ROME, (AP)—Douglas Fairbanks and Lady Sylvia Ashley arranged today to take an extended trip to the West Indies. - Following their arrival here today from St. Moritz, they asked that reservations be made for them on a liner leaving Marseille for Trinidad. It was learned that at Trinidad they will embark on a West Indian cruise aboard a yacht Fairbanks has chartered. A young English couple, named Chisholm, who came here with the actor and Lady Ashley are understood to be planning to accompany them on the cruise.

1935-07-03.text: Bucharest, Roumania, July 3, (WP) — A court summons ordering former King George of Greece to appear in the divorce court Saturday to answer a petition of former Queen Elizabeth for divorce was published in the official gazette today. Former King George was in London today, and was not expected to leave by Saturday. It was believed he would be represented by counsel in the divorce court. Friends said that politically the suit was without significance. A divorce, they asserted, would not affect George’s chances of enthronement because high connections in Greece had long known a divorce was probable but arranged his return nevertheless.

Wimbledon, Eng., July 3. (CP)—Baron Gottfried von Cramm, German Davis cup player, eliminated Donald Budge of Oakland, Calif., today to gain the final round of the all-England singles’ tennis championship with Fred Perry, the defending titleholder. After putting up a remarkable offensive against the German player in the first two sets, Budge fell into errors and was set down in four sets, 4-6, 6-4, 6-3, 6-2. Perry accounted for his arch British Empire foe, Jack Crawford of Australia, whom he met in the final of last year’s championship. The black-haired English star split the first two sets with Crawford and then crowded on pressure to close out against him the fourth, winning by scores of 6-2, 3-6, 6-4, 6-4.

LONDON, July 3. (AP)—Great Britain has decided to try to placate France by reaffirming its agreement with the French argument that Europe's problems must be settled as an interdependent whole, it was reported on excellent authority today. Notably such a decision would mean agreement with the French demand that an aerial defense league embracing France, Britain, Italy, Belgium and Germany should be negotiated only as part of a general political agreement. The cabinet met today and was reported to have discussed sending a note designed to elicit present views on the Italian-Abyssinian crisis, especially the attitude France will take before the League of Nations when the crisis is considered. France's policy has been regarded here as favorable to Italy’s assertion of overlordship in Abyssinia—a policy which would tend to increase French-British estrangement arising from the British-German n

LONDON, July 3.--(P)--A Reuters (British) news agency dispatch from Peiping said that five persons were executed secretly at dawn today for participation in the attack by mutinous soldiers last Friday on Peiping.

London, July 6. (INS).—Great Britain's lack of faith in the arms limitations clauses of the Versailles treaty was made known officially by Sir Samuel Hoare, foreign minister, in a statement to the House of Commons. Britain, Sir Samuel said, sees no prospect of a general international naval agreement on the basis of the qualitative and quantitative limitation clauses of the Versailles pact. In view of this, Sir Samuel declined to give assurance that Britain would proceed in general naval disarmament negotiations on the basis of the Versailles restrictions imposed on Germany.

NAPLES, July 3 (AP) — Mount Vesuvius erupted with a tremendous explosion early today, blowing a piece of its cone from the crater high into the air. The explosion tore an aperture in the cone from which lava was flowing copiously. Soon afterward, another opening appeared at the base of the cone. The explosion occurred before daybreak, and the discharge of burning lava and sparks lighted up the heavens for miles. Residents of Naples rushed to their windows in alarm at the roar of the eruption. Lava also was flowing from the opening at the base of the cone.

Addis Ababa, July 3.—(AP)—Unconfirmed reports today said that heavy casualties had been sustained in a battle between Italian and Ethiopian forces on the frontier of Eritrea. No details were immediately available. At the same time, it was reported that 5,000,000 cartridges consigned to Ethiopia from Belgium were being held up at the seaport of Djibouti, French Somaliland, by French authorities.

BERLIN, July 3. (P)—The Nazi executioner swung his ax twice today, decapitating two Germans convicted of espionage. Those convicted were Egon Bresz, 28, who was convicted of having tried to obtain military secrets of the Reich, and Bruno Hindemann, 63, who betrayed military information. Both were tried in the people’s court, which also sentenced Wilhelm Battesch, 48, to life imprisonment for betraying military information.

LONDON, April 30.—Britain tonight seemed veering definitely toward union with those nations openly opposed to Germany's swift, surprising rearmament. This was the situation foreseen by competent quarters as proposed Anglo-German naval conversations stood “adjourned” until after Adolf Hitler's statement on foreign policy expected May 15. These quarters declared it was now up to Hitler to make the next move if he hoped to keep Great Britain in her role of “good neighbor” and “honest broker” as concerns the continent's troubles. Await Hitler Statement While French officials openly voiced hopes of negotiating bilateral air agreements with England, Italy and Belgium and the authoritative Italian newspaper Giornale D’Italia laid bare Germany’s asserted “big navy” program for 1935-1938, the British government fixed its attention on Hitler’s forthcoming statement. LONDON, (Copyright by AP). Great Britain, an authoritative source revealed, will spend an extra $25,000,000 this year to keep abreast of Germany in Europe's headlong air armament race. That amount will be expended in addition to the 105 millions already provided in air estimates for the current fiscal year, the informed source disclosed. The proposal, regarded in informed quarters as an answer to Adolf Hitler's boast that the Reich now is as strong in the air as Great Britain, is expected to be the highlight of Prime Minister MacDonald's “important announcement” opening the House of Commons debate on foreign affairs Thursday. MacDonald, speaking in the House of Commons, said flatly the British government stood behind an article he wrote last week assailing Germany's swift rearmament as perilous to the continent's peace. A ringing assertion by Winston Churchill, fiery conservative, that German air superiority already exists featured the debate that followed upon Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald’s announcement the government “already is taking steps” toward expanding British air strength. Just what the expansion program involved MacDonald did not reveal, but informed sources said earlier the government stood ready to spend $25,000,000 in addition to the $105,000,000 already provided in this year’s air estimates. LONDON, May 1 (#)—Europe’s once pastoral festival of May Day, ushered in by bombs and skirmishes that took four lives in various countries, developed under stern police precautions into a peaceful observance of the international Labor day. Moscow displayed her military might before Joseph Stalin, Russia’s “man of steel,” and Reichsfuehrer Adolf Hitler exhorted to peace nearly a million of his people gathered in a gigantic demonstration at the Tempelhof Airdrome, Berlin. Elsewhere, the day for the most part was one of festivities—free goulash in Vienna, quiet meetings in Paris, uneventful dances and concerts in Italy, a “fashion parade” of well-dressed working men in Stockholm, and jubilee preparations in England. At the same time it was reported to have decided on a new effort to win the Reich’s cooperation in a general security system based on disarmament. Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald was expected to lay this program before the House of Commons with an announcement that Great Britain's air program will be accelerated and expanded. To Redeem Pledge The enlarged aerial defense plans, which would redeem the pledge made in 1934 by Stanley Baldwin to keep Great Britain's air force ahead of that of any other nearby power, were said by an authoritative source to contemplate the expenditure this year of $25,000,000 more than the $105,000,000 already provided for 1933. London, May 2—(U. P.)—Great Britain already has begun to build up her air force to meet the aerial expansion of Germany, Prime Minister J. Ramsay MacDonald declared in the House of Commons today, in a general exposition of Britain’s position toward averting war in Europe. MacDonald said that the German naval program was in violation of the Versailles treaty.

London, May 2.—Formally announcing expansion and acceleration of Britain's air building program to match the ships and guns of a re-arming Europe, Prime Minister J. Ramsay MacDonald today issued an impassioned appeal to Germany to join with the other powers in a general peace settlement. Addressing the House of Commons when debate began on German re-armament, MacDonald pleaded for cooperation in a general new agreement to supplant the outworn arms clauses of the treaty of Versailles.

1935-11-18.text: LONDON, Nov. 18.—(AP)—League of Nations economic sanctions, approved by 51 nations, took effect against Italy today in an unprecedented effort to force a halt to war. These nations virtually severed financial and trading relations with the invaders of Ethiopia, pledging themselves to exclude Italian goods from their markets and to cease supplying Italy with a selected list of raw materials. "Theoretically, the economic blockade was imposed at one minute after midnight, but practically, it developed that legal aspects delayed slightly some nations. Portugal took the lead, closing its frontiers to Italian goods and halting export of raw materials which might be used for warfare as early as Saturday. France faced a possible delay in enforcement of economic sanctions, but this apparently was reduced, if not eliminated, by publication yesterday of boycott decrees. These decrees forbade import

CAIRO, Nov. 18 (Py) — Riotous students stormed through the streets today in defiance of police. They were again protesting British influence in government. Eight hundred rushed the gates of the government hospital. They had heard a student injured in a riot last week had died and wanted his body. Police held the mob at bay by firing blank shots until British reserves and native police arrived to ride them down. The reinforcements rode into the mob striking out with the flat sides of their sabres and drove the demonstrators into side streets where the students massed again to shout: “Off with the British yoke! Long live nationalism.”

LONDON, Nov. 17—(AP)—The League of Nations threw the strength of half a hundred nations behind an economic boycott of Italy at midnight tonight but Benito Mussolini, digging in defiantly for the siege, warned in the boycott, orchestrated in Geneva in an effort to force an early end to Italy’s war on Ethiopia, have pledged themselves: 1. To buy nothing whatsoever from Italy. 2. To send to Italy none of certain “key products” essential to the manufacture of arms and munitions of war. The economic wall that Great Britain, France and the other League powers thus have built around Italy constitutes the major part of the sanctions program applied under the League Covenant. The British express horror and surprise that thousands of educated young Egyptian students should be included in a mob in Cairo throwing stones, breaking British windows, and demanding Egyptian independence, free of English control. Those young men, who would not run away until bird shot was fired at them, know that Egypt, under British control, has had the nearest approach to honest government that she has known since Cleopatra and long before. In Egypt, today, the poorest of the fellahin can obtain justice from the richest Egyptian before a British judge. The number of blind children has been greatly reduced, the British have discouraged the Egyptian mother's theory that it is sinful to brush disease-carrying flies from the inflamed eyelids of her baby because its great grandmother's spirit might be residing in one of the flies. By International News Service Italy struck back with speed and determination today as over 50 nations launched the first great collective effort to halt a war by coercion, and Britain and other leading spirits in League of Nations sanctions hastened to plug in the economic and financial siege wall encircling Italy. While more fighting was reported on the Ethiopian front, and new commander, Marshal Pietro Badoglio, prepared to leave to inject new life into the campaign, Italy halted imports from sanctionist nations, hitting first at France, and demonstrations in Italian cities proclaimed Italy’s resolution to boycott sanctionists. Negotiations for certificates of origin on goods to Egypt, where student demonstrations against Britain, in connection with funerals of those slain last week, continued, and Italian goods were still being handled.

Tokyo, Nov. 18 (#) — Japanese dispatches from Peiping and Tientsin unanimously and unreservedly announced tonight that a new nation, that of North China, will be born this week. These dispatches, by the Rengo agency among others, state that the new nation, like Manchoukuo, will be created under the protection of Japan’s mighty military machine which the Chinese National government at Nanking is powerless to oppose. It seemed likely that five more provinces of China would follow the fate of the four Manchurian provinces which at present form Japan’s protectorate, the Empire of Manchoukuo.
